### `cloud eval list`

List the eval suites saved in a project.

| Flag | Required | Des
cription |\n| - | - | - |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project) |\

n
### `cloud eval run`

Start an eval run of an existing suite, or upload a versioned suite file and run it. Provide **either**
`--suite` **or** `--file`, not both.\n\nBy default the command prints a launch receipt and returns immediately. `--wait` polls ev
ery launched run to a terminal state.\n\n**Exit codes (`--wait` only).** Without `--wait` this command's exit code is unchanged: `
0` on any launch, `1` on a partial or wholly failed fan-out. `--wait` owns a separate six-code contract — a caller who asked this

process to sit and watch a run to completion is asking it to say how the run went:

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Every
waited run passed, unanimously, and (when a report was requested) every report was assembled |\n| `1` | A run **completed** with
a **failed** verdict. The only condition that produces this code |\n| `2` | Usage error — bad flags, `--reporter`/`--out` without
`--wait`, or an invalid suite file (after auth, before any server/model work) |\n| `3` | Auth failed — no credential, or the platf
orm rejected it, at launch or mid-wait (a token that expired during a long poll). Zero credits spent if it happened before launch
|\n| `4` | Connection/setup failed before evaluation — a launch failure this CLI itself observed (network, timeout, rate limit, a
partial or failed fan-out, an unrecognized launch error), or a local `--out` write failure — unless a more severe outcome (`1` or
`3`) already applies to the same run, per the merge order above |\n| `5` | No valid verdict — `inconclusive`, a null/unrecognized
result, a run whose own status is failed/cancelled/timed-out, a wait that hit its deadline, a mid-wait failure that was not auth-s
haped, or a report that could not be assembled |\n\nNo infrastructure condition ever maps to `1` — see the same rule under `eval g
ate` below. A multi-target launch merges these worst-of across every waited run, in the order `1 > 3 > 4 > 5 > 0`: a real verdict
failure is never masked by a sibling's infrastructure noise, and a credential failure (which may be *why* other targets show no ve
rdict) outranks a plain connection failure.\n\nThis six-code contract is new and deliberately **different** from `eval gate`'s fou
r codes below — see that command's own doc for why the two are not unified. An invalid suite file exits **2** either way — `eval v
alidate` still exits 1 for the same contract failure, because it is a verdict on the file and this command is not.\n\n| Flag | Req

uired | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--suite <id-or-name>` | Yes, unless `--file` | Eval suite name or ID |
| `--file <path>`
| Yes, unless `--suite` | Versioned suite file to upload and run (`.yaml` or `.json`, or `-` for stdin) |\n| `--project <id-or-na
me>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project) |\n| `--server <id-or-name...>` | No | Override the
suite's saved server selection (HTTP servers only) |\n| `--environment <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached project environment(s) to
run. Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--client <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached client(s) to run, so the run is
stamped with that client's config. Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--host <id-or-name...>` | No | **Deprecated**
alias for `--client`. Passing both is an error. Not the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam compat --host` / `mcpjam tools --host` tak
e — see [Two different `--host` flags](#two-different---host-flags). |\n| `--all-targets` | No | Run **every** attached environmen
t (or, if none, every attached host) — one **paid run per target** |\n| `--iterations <n>` | No | Run each case this many times (1
-10), for this run only |\n| `--repetitions <n>` | No | **Legacy** spelling of `--iterations`. Passing both is an error. |\n| `--c
ase <id-or-title...>` | No | Run only these cases instead of the whole suite |\n| `--exclude-skills` | No | Run the \"without skil
ls\" A/B arm: nothing is pinned, and the run is labelled as excluded |\n| `--refresh-snapshot` | No | **Persists a new host-config
snapshot on the suite** (see below). Single-target runs only. |\n| `--notes <text>` | No | Free-text note stored on the run |\n|
`--min-pass-rate <n>` | No | Pass threshold for this run (0-100), overriding the suite's own |\n| `--match-options <json>` | No |
Tool-call match options for this run, e.g. `'{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'` |\n| `--idempotency-key <key>` | No | Retry key for a
lost launch response. For `--file`, a fresh key is minted and printed on every invocation when this flag is omitted; supply the p
rinted key to replay the same run instead of starting a new one |\n| `--wait` | No | Wait for every launched run to reach a termin
al status |\n| `--wait-timeout <ms>` | No | Maximum wait time (default 2100000); requires `--wait` |\n| `--reporter <json-summary\
\|junit-xml\\|html>` | No | Write the completed structured report to stdout; requires `--wait`. `html` is a self-contained decisio
n summary + failures page — traces/parity/history are not included. |\n| `--out <path>` | No | Atomically write the completed repo
rt to a file; defaults to `json-summary`, or uses `--reporter` when present; requires `--wait` |\n| `--compose-client <id-or-name>
` | No | Compose a stack to run instead of naming a saved environment (see below). **Ephemeral by default** — pass `--save-targets
` to attach it to the suite. |\n| `--compose-host <id-or-name>` | No | **Deprecated** alias for `--compose-client` |\n| `--compose
-computer <id-or-name>` | No | Sandbox image to pin on the composed stack |\n| `--compose-model <id...>` | No | Model(s) to run on
the composed stack. Replaces the client's pinned model unless `--with-client-default` is set |\n| `--compose-model-selection <jso
n...>` | No | Whole saved model selection(s) — source, connection, `settings.reasoningEffort` — as JSON: one cell per selection, f
or its model, at its effort. Repeat to add several selections for one model (e.g. at low and at high) — each distinct selection is
its own cell |\n| `--with-client-default` | No | Also launch an inherit cell using each client's pinned model, alongside `--compo
se-model` |\n| `--compose-server <id-or-name...>` | No | Server(s) to pin on the composed stack, snapshotted into a server group s
o a rerun keeps testing them. Mutually exclusive with `--compose-server-group` |\n| `--compose-server-group <id>` | No | Standalon
